A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FMPlug research by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration, image-regression, LIS, MRI, and ablation results. Its separately attributed Red-Diff reference scores do not affect this assessment.

after.justification: v2 retains original restoration experiments and reports revised scientific results, black-hole imaging, sensitivity studies, computational measurements, and repeated-initialization experiments.

M1.justification: v2's stated method and complete algorithms omit v1's additional mean–variance calibration, which used 4000 generated samples and a fitted network (v1 Section 3.1). The central learned warm-start, Gaussian shell projection, and softmax-weighted few-shot guidance remain. The PDFs do not establish whether calibration was also removed from the computations underlying retained results.

E1.justification: v2 adds black-hole imaging using nonlinear VLBI measurements with non-additive noise, substantially extending scientific coverage beyond LIS and MRI. The three natural-image datasets and four restoration tasks remain. The higher-noise calibration experiment from v1 is absent.

E2.justification: The comparator roster remains DIP, D-Flow, FlowDPS, FlowChef, OT-ODE, PnP-Flow, and the quoted Red-Diff reference. Unprompted variants omitted from v2's main Table 3 remain in its appendix. The domain-specific comparison moves from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 16; black-hole imaging extends the existing scientific comparator set.

E3.justification: New protocols include black-hole evaluation with 100 targets, five guidance images, and closure-consistency metrics, plus parameter sweeps and runtime/memory measurements. Retained settings also receive explicit revisions: DIP's optimizer changes from Adam to AdamW, and Appendix A.2 describes the regression run as FMPlug rather than FMPlug-W. These are reported setting changes, without proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablation, v2 tests learned warm-start time versus blur severity, shell thickness, NFE, random initialization, and MRI guidance-set size. It also analyzes guidance-weight correlations and illustrates MRI guidance mismatch. These substantially expand mechanism and robustness evidence (Sections 4.2–4.3 and A.7). Conversely, v1's calibration ablation at two noise levels is removed.

E5.justification: v2 adds ten random initializations per image on a DIV2K subset and reports mean-plus-variability entries for four methods in Table 17; v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. It also reports Pearson and Spearman correlations for MRI guidance weights. This statistical reporting is localized: principal benchmark tables still lack uncertainty, and the aggregation behind the quantities called variances is insufficiently specified.

E6.justification: Scientific results are substantially revised: FMPlug's LIS PSNR/SSIM changes from 31.83/0.97 to 34.65/0.91, while MRI SSIM changes from beating DIP, 0.48 versus 0.39, to trailing it, 0.52 versus 0.54. v2 adds black-hole results, including FMPlug PSNR 22.91, and numerous diagnostic results. These are revised reports, not established same-setting improvements. Restoration tables and the relocated domain-specific comparison retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.6 explicitly identifies the original scattering expression as nonlinear and introduces the first Born assumption and resulting linear equation. It also adds black-hole visibility and closure-measurement mathematics. The Gaussian concentration theorem and core shell argument remain unchanged; the added indicator-function expression merely restates the existing constraint.

C1.justification: The central contributions—identifying weak foundation priors and strengthening them through instance guidance and Gaussian regularization—remain. v2's abstract and contribution list emphasize scientific few-shot applications more explicitly, and its new conclusion claims scientific performance often approaches domain-specific priors, extending v1's scientific-results framing of substantial remaining gaps.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies scientific performance as comparable to or better than DIP, replacing v1's large-margin superiority interpretation. It explains MRI limitations through inadequate guidance coverage, states why two InverseBench tasks are excluded, interprets learned weights and parameter sensitivity, and discusses speed–quality tradeoffs. It also newly treats no-reference metrics as secondary indicators and explains that choice.

D1.justification: v2 adds two algorithm listings, sigmoid time parameterization and initialization, explicit latent encoding, dimension-matching instructions, gradient checkpointing, black-hole measurement details, and a project-page link. These substantially improve implementation documentation without necessarily introducing new procedures. Some earlier information disappears, including calibration construction and D-Flow's initialization guidance scale.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting scientific data/computation constraints and discussion of no-reference metric reliability, including Bommasani, Chua, Chen, Antsiferova, Liao, and Rasheed. It removes the citation acknowledging the preliminary Wan et al. version. Positioning against the established FM inverse-problem methods otherwise remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the original exposition remains, with wording edits and expanded scientific motivation. v2 separates implementation issues into Section 3.3, reorganizes appendix sections, moves the domain-specific comparison into Appendix A.5, and adds a conclusion and impact statement. These refine the existing narrative rather than comprehensively rewriting it.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main paper to a two-column layout, replaces the opening conceptual diagram, adds scientific-guidance illustrations and diagnostic tables, and expands qualitative comparisons with marked regions and enlarged crops. Main Table 3 is shortened while its full comparisons remain in the appendix. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the scientific few-shot contribution: black-hole imaging, guidance-count and weight analyses, sensitivity studies, and repeated initializations address applicability and mechanisms that v1 scarcely tested. Pseudocode, implementation explanations, MRI failure analysis, and efficiency measurements also make the work easier to assess and reproduce. Gains are tempered by lost calibration evidence, unexplained LIS/MRI score replacements, and an overbroad stability claim—Table 17 gives FlowChef lower LPIPS variability than FMPlug. Nevertheless, the added diagnostic evidence and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net quality improvement.
